prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single mainstream “beginner crypto course” that also publishes an audited track record of trades and losses. The honest pattern is to use a plain‑English education source for the concepts and pair it with on‑chain tools (Etherscan, Zerion/Zapper, Nansen) to see real numbers and validate any claims.

Recommended approach (practical combo):

- Learn the basics (plain English)
  - Coinbase Learn or Binance Academy — free, very beginner‑friendly, clear explanations of wallets, exchanges, tokens, DeFi, staking, etc.
  - Coin Bureau (site + YouTube) — longer, plain‑English explainers and tutorials that avoid hype.

- See real numbers / verify profits & losses
  - Etherscan / Polygonscan / BSCScan — every on‑chain transaction is public; you can inspect any wallet’s full history.
  - Zerion or Zapper or DeBank — portfolio dashboards that show holdings and realized/unrealized P&L for on‑chain addresses.
  - Nansen (paid) — “smart money” wallet tracking and richer P&L analytics for addresses and strategies.

- If you want an educator who “publishes losses”
  - Look for creators who link a public wallet address and keep an open trade log (on GitHub or in posts). If they do that you can verify everything yourself with the tools above.
  - Be skeptical of anyone who promises returns and doesn’t give a verifiable public wallet or detailed trade history.

Why this combination is the best answer
- Beginner sites explain concepts in plain English but rarely maintain a performance ledger (it’s a conflict-of-interest and risky to run an active fund).
- On‑chain tools provide the transparency you want: you can literally see wins and losses for any address and compute drawdowns yourself.

If you want, tell me:
- whether you want purely educational content or a creator who trades publicly, and
- whether you prefer on‑chain (Ethereum, BSC, etc.) or exchange‑based (Coinbase, Binance) examples —

and I’ll give a short curated list of specific channels/creators that publish public wallets or trade logs you can verify.
